notes: Korea's biggest carrier (~half of domestic parcel volume) and the main last-mile partner for AliExpress/Cainiao imports. Uses 12 digits most of the time; sources disagree on whether 10 and 13 digits also occur. Plain digits collide with Hanjin and Lotte (12 digits). Community sources report a check digit (last digit = first 11 digits mod 7) that is shared with Lotte and Logen. Use it as a ranking boost, not a filter. The example is built to satisfy that rule. Strip hyphens/spaces before matching (labels print it as 1234-5678-9012). The CJ app (오네) auto-registers CJ parcels by phone number. The id follows tracker.delivery naming.

Hanjin's customer guide says 10–12 digits; in practice 10 or 12. Main domestic carrier for Temu Korea (2024 reports) and a secondary carrier for AliExpress. Fully ambiguous with CJ/Lotte, so rank by user history, by the shop (Temu → Hanjin), and by a live probe. Tracking URL is best-effort and should be verified.
Formerly 현대택배 (Hyundai Logistics). 12 digits. Reportedly uses the same mod-7 check digit as CJ (unverified); the example satisfies it. Ambiguous with CJ and Hanjin.

Domestic parcels (소포) and registered mail (등기) use 13 digits. Sources agree on the length, and 13 digits is the strongest single signal for Korea Post. Daesin (13) and some CJ/Logen numbers can also be 13 digits, so keep the alternatives as candidates. Korea Post is also a fallback last-mile carrier for AliExpress. Example is illustrative.

UPU S10 format: 2 letters, 8-digit serial, 1 check digit, ISO country code. EMS uses the E? prefix. The check digit uses weights 8,6,4,2,3,5,9,7, then c = 11 - (sum mod 11), with 10→0 and 11→5. Validate it to reject typos. The example passes.
S10 numbers ending in KR, other than the EMS (E?) prefix. Common prefixes: R? registered, L? untracked/ePacket-like, C? parcel post, V? insured. Same check-digit algorithm as EMS.

Usually 11 digits. Several guides say '11 digits → Logen first; 12 → CJ/Hanjin/Lotte'. One Q&A also mentions 13 digits. Reported mod-7 check digit (first 10 digits mod 7 = last), unverified. The example satisfies it.

No reliable length found; the regex is a deliberately broad catch-all. Kyungdong often delivers to a branch (영업소) where the recipient picks up, so the 'arrived at branch' status maps to AvailableForPickup. Common for furniture and bulky items. Only suggest it when the user picks it or a probe confirms.
Branch-pickup carrier like Kyungdong. Same 13-digit length as Korea Post, so rank it below Korea Post unless the user picked it. URL is best-effort.

Store-to-store (반값택배) parcels end at a store, and the 'store arrival' (점포 도착) status is AvailableForPickup. The pickup QR code arrives by KakaoTalk 알림톡 or SMS. CU 편의점택배 (CU Post) has a similar flow and no confirmed format. URL is best-effort.

Rocket Delivery (로켓배송) runs on Coupang's own logistics (CLS). The tracking number is often hidden or shown only under 주문상세 → 자세히 보기. One blog says it is 14 digits; this is unverified. A 2026 blog says coupangls.com supports tracking without login, but no public URL template was confirmed. Coupang's in-app tracker already shows the current location, a time window, and a delivery-completion photo, so users rarely need a third-party tracker for Rocket orders. Coupang Marketplace (non-Rocket) orders use normal carriers (CJ, Hanjin, Lotte, Korea Post). Treat this candidate as 'open the Coupang app' unless an API covers it (tracker.delivery lists kr.coupangls; verify).

Generic S10 rule. The last two letters are the origin postal operator's ISO country code (CN, KR, US, JP, GB…). Check digit: weights 8,6,4,2,3,5,9,7; c = 11 - (sum mod 11); 10→0, 11→5. Route to the country-specific entry when one exists. When the parcel reaches Korea it is usually handed to Korea Post (same number) for postal items.

S10 ending in CN. The prefix tells the service: L? = ePacket/small packet (often used by AliExpress sellers), R? = registered, C? = parcel, E? = China EMS. China Post has no stable public deep link, so use 17TRACK as the fallback page. Numbers are usually unchanged when Korea Post takes over in Korea.
This is a subset of cn.chinapost. When both match, prefer this entry.

AliExpress Standard/economy numbers usually look like 'LP' + 14 digits. Some sources show variants with a CN suffix, and Cainiao also issues other prefixes (e.g. CAINIAO…, AEKR-style marketplace ids), so this regex is not exhaustive. In Korea the parcel enters via Pyeongtaek/Incheon, clears customs, and is then handed to CJ대한통운 (~80% historically) or Hanjin, Lotte, or Korea Post. A new domestic number is issued at that point. Linking the LP number to the domestic number is the single most valuable cross-border feature.
Common for Temu, SHEIN, and dropship stores. 'YT' + 16 digits is the dominant pattern, but at least one source claims 13-character variants. The last-mile number in Korea changes after handover.
Mixed formats. '4PX…CN' is the most recognizable one; other 4PX numbers are opaque.
SF numbers are 'SF' + 12–13 digits; older all-digit 12-digit numbers also exist and collide with Korean carriers. SF often asks for the last 4 digits of the recipient phone number to show details.
'1Z' + 6-character shipper account + 2-digit service code + 7-digit reference + 1 check digit. Highly distinctive. UPS Mail Innovations and SurePost numbers can look like USPS numbers.

Express is 12 digits, Ground 15, and SmartPost/Ground Economy 20–22 (overlaps USPS). 12 digits collides with every major Korean carrier. Only suggest FedEx for a 12-digit number if the order is cross-border (Amazon US, iHerb) or the user chose it. 15 digits is fairly distinctive.

Domestic IMpb numbers are 20–22 digits starting 91–95, and barcodes may carry a 420+ZIP prefix. Strip it, or accept it as this regex does. International numbers are S10 ending in US. Arrivals to Korea are handed to Korea Post with the same S10 number.

DHL Express waybills are 10 digits, which collides with CJ/Hanjin 10-digit numbers. Don't rank DHL first for a KR user unless context says international. DHL eCommerce/Parcel use other formats (JJD…, GM…, 00340…) that are not covered here. DHL Express imports to Korea are delivered by DHL itself, so the number does not change.

Used only for Amazon's own last mile (US/EU/JP). Amazon Global shipments to Korea usually travel via UPS/DHL/FedEx and are handed to a Korean carrier, so the user should track that carrier's number instead.
